name: ENKI Value Lattice Vocabulary Pack
description: Defines how VALUES live in the substrate. A value is a first-class node (gets its own base60 address) that lives inside its property's lattice. Values refine other values via a partial order; depth comes from precisionvocab; cycle comes from propertyvocab. This pack carries the LATTICE MECHANICS (how refines/subsumes/conflicts work) and the BOOTSTRAP CHAINS (initial value seeds for high-traffic properties: location, time, language). New value chains can be admitted at runtime via the gateway — this pack only seeds what the substrate needs to function on day one. Forward-compat: bootstrap chains are immutable identifiers; future versions add more chains or extend existing chains downward (deeper) but never reorder.

metadata.author: ENKI System
forward_compat_rules: Bootstrap chain IDs are immutable. 'location.country.US' in v0.1.0 stays 'location.country.US' forever.
Chains can be extended downward (deeper) without a major bump — adding 'location.address.123_main_st' under 'location.city.springfield' is safe.
Chains cannot be reordered or have intermediate levels removed within a minor version.
Runtime admission of values is allowed and expected — the bootstrap chains are seeds, not exhaustive enumerations.
Value normalization rules (e.g. 'red' = 'RED' = 'Red') stay stable within minor versions.
